lines: caveman
/ˈ k  e  ɪ v m æ n /
▪(数千年前的)穴居人 someone who lived in a cave many
thousands of years ago
▪a man who is rude or violent, and has old-fashioned
ideas 蛮的人; 粗的人
1 The caveman had to make do with primitive
tools to hunt for food. L41
2 Don't be such a caveman! Use a napkin
instead of wiping your hands on your pants.
3 The recent discovery shed light on the daily
activities of cavemen. L38

/ p ɒ t //ˈ h ə ʊ l ɪ ŋ /

solitude n.
/ˈs ɒ l ɪ t j u ː d /
1 The solitude of a quiet forest can be a
catastrophe for someone accustomed to city
life. L33

spiritual matters in solitude. L5&L37

of solitude before the pressures of the day
began.
lure v.
/ l ʊ ə /
1 The possibility of success can often lure
people into taking risks they might avoid. N2L44
2 He attempted to lure her away from her
husband and family. L8
3 What invariably happens is that short videos
can easily lure adults away from their daily routine.
pot-holer n.
/ p ɒ t //həʊlə/
1 The experienced pot-holer took advantage
of his advanced climbing skills to explore
deeper into the cave. L37
2 What became of the missing pot-holer was
a mystery until he finally emerged from a hidden
cave. L36&L35
3 The pot-holers consulted the map to ensure
they were on the right path. L37
rambler n.
/ˈræm.bl ə/
▪someone who goes for walks in the countryside for
pleasure 〔在乡间的〕闲逛者,漫步者
1 As a passionate rambler, she spent her
weekends hiking through the mountains. N2L59
2 At the mere mention of a fantastic new
destination, the rambler went into raptures. L41
3 Today the railway attracts many tourists to
the area, and is very popular with ramblers.
N2L94
undertaking n.
/ʌn.dəˈteɪ.kɪŋ/
▪an important job, piece of work, or activity that you are
responsible for〔要的〕任务;事业
1 She is conscious that starting a new business
can be a risky undertaking. L31
2 It suddenly dawned on me that it might be
a more difficult undertaking than it appears at
first sight. L37
3 It is anticipated that the trip across country
was a dangerous undertaking. L26
foresight n.
/ˈfɔː.saɪt/
▪the ability to imagine what is likely to happen and to
consider this when planning for the future
先见之明,远见;深谋远虑
▪have the foresight to do
1 He had the foresight to swerve to avoid the
accident. L39
2 It has always been a mystery to me why they
had the foresight to invest in the new technology.
3 If you had had more foresight to change

foretell foretold
/ f ɔ ː ˈ t e l // f ɔ ː ˈ t ə ʊ l d /
▪to say what will happen in the future, especially by using
special magical powers〔尤指用超凡的能力〕预言
1 I have developed an unshakable belief in the
idea that nobody could foretell the future. L37
2 The ancient prophecy foretold the rise of a
great leader who would bring about the downfall
of previous cruel ruler. L36
3 The mere fact [that the fortune teller foretold
a promotion in his future] gave him hope and
motivation to work harder. L34
Grenoble n.
/ g r ə ˈ n o ʊ b ə l /
1 格勒诺布尔
chasm n.
/ˈ k æ z ə m /
▪a very deep space between two areas of rock or ice,
especially one that is dangerous
〔尤指危险的〕裂隙,深坑,深渊
1 To be reunited with the team, the hiker knew
he had to be prepared to cross the chasm that
lay ahead. L36
2 What a relief it was when the rescue team
arrived just in time to save the climbers from
falling into the chasm. L39
3 The children went into raptures as they
watched the hiker fearlessly cross the chasm.
flaw n.
/fɔː/
▪a break, scratch, crack, etc. that spoils something 小裂缝...
1 The expert immediately noticed a small flaw
in the antique vase and noted with satisfaction
that it would increase its value. L37
2 It is odd that the new car had a flaw in its
paintwork, but the company promised that it
would be fixed. L37
distinguished adj.
/dɪˈstɪŋɡ wɪʃt/
▪successful, respected, and admired 杰出的; 著名的; 卓越的
1 The distinguished professor conducted the
new student to the library. L37
2 She described to me what the distinguished
visitor looked like. L34
3 He seems to have a fascination for
distinguished philosopher. L34
4 He asked me to keep an eye on the
distinguished guests. L33
Everest n.
/ˈe v ə r ɪ s t /
1 珠穆朗玛峰
wade v.
/weɪd/
▪to walk through water that is not deep 蹚(水),涉(水)
▪wade through/across 蹚过
1 There was a note of triumph in his voice
when he said he had managed to wade across
the stream. L37 N2L67
2 Have you heard of anyone who was able to
wade through this kind of deep mud? L37 N2L43
3 There was a chance that he failed to wade
through the river and died at last. L36 N2L16
waterfall n.
/ˈwɔːtəfɔːl/
1 The mere fact [that the waterfall is surrounded
by sweet-smelling trees] attracted me to travel
miles to get there. L34&L41
2 You could only go on foot to reach the
hidden waterfall. L31

waterfall mysteriously disappeared overnight.

/ˈr ʌ b ə l /
▪〔被毁的建筑物或墙壁的〕碎石,碎砖,瓦砾

insistent adj.
/ ɪ nˈs ɪ s . t ə n t /
1 反复的;再三的;持续不断的;
2 Oddly enough, there was an insistent knock

boom v.
/ b u ː m  /
▪to make a loud deep sound 发出低沉的声音,隆隆作响

waterspout n.
/ˈw ɔ ː . t ə . s p a ʊ t /

2 He presumed that the booming sound was
from a waterspout in the cave. L36
3 I couldn't believe my eyes when a waterspout

cleft n.

1 (自然的)裂口,裂缝;
